The Dolphins (1-7) beat the Jets in Week 7 to scuttle early speculation that they would go without a victory this season, and now they face a Colts team that is on a five-game losing streak and sits at 2-7. Now Willis is on IR, so Kyle McCord will get the start Sunday. Only the Chargers score fewer points than Miami, but the Dolphins have been solid at times on defense. They rank 13th in yards allowed but are 22nd in scoring defense, while the Indianapolis offense is 24th in scoring and the defense is 30th in points allowed. Jones led the team to a 7-1 start last season, but he hasn't been the same this season. A five-game losing streak that includes a loss to the now 1-7 Titans has the Colts selling off important parts. Jones has 1,077 passing yards, with 10 interceptions against six TD passes, and Indy is tied for the worst turnover margin in the league at minus-11. Miami is minus-3. Still, the SportsLine model has the Colts winning at home in 68% of its simulations.

Jones was being discussed as an MVP candidate before he went down last season, but now with Josh Downs  and  Keenan Allen  gone, tight end  Tyler Warren  is his top pass-catcher.
